answer.location_description: A full-image horizontal stripe (grating) pattern covering every row and column: alternating 2-pixel-high horizontal bands with a 4-row period. Rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 form one phase; rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 form the opposite phase.
answer.shortcut_type: periodic horizontal stripe / scan-line artifact texture
answer.mechanism: Eight layer-1 units are horizontal-grating detectors, and they come in two opposite-phase groups. Group B (units 12, 13, 23, 29) has large negative biases (about -56 to -88). Their weights are positive on rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, ... and negative on rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, ..., so they fire only when the image has bright bands in that phase. These units feed positively into layer-2 units 0, 8, 10 and 14, which have large positive output weights (85, 62, 76, 90), so they push the logit toward malignant. Group A (units 2, 11, 17, 25) has the opposite phase and large positive biases (74-99). It feeds layer-2 units 9 and 11 (output weights -99 and -66), which push toward benign. The same group-A units also strongly inhibit u0, u8, u10 and u14 (e.g. unit 17 -> u10 = -96, u14 = -87). A stripe pattern in the group-B phase therefore drives the logit positive.
answer.evidence: The structured hidden units 2, 11, 12, 13, 17, 23, 25 and 29 have near-constant weight values along entire rows (all 24 columns) that alternate sign every 2 rows. For example, unit 23 has rows 0-1 at about +30, rows 2-3 at about -25, rows 4-5 at about +35, rows 6-7 at about -45, and so on down to rows 20-21 at about +40. Unit 2 shows the mirror image. A real nodule feature would be centred and roughly radial, not a uniform 4-row-period grating spanning the edges and corners of the crop. Lung CT anatomy also does not produce such a regular grating. The other 24 hidden units look like unstructured noise. Layer 2 sorts the two phases cleanly. u0, u8, u10 and u14 take strongly positive weights from units 12, 13, 23 and 29 (e.g. u8: 99, 73) and negative weights from units 2, 11, 17 and 25 (e.g. u8: -51, -31, -80, -42). u9 and u11 show the reverse pattern. The output weights are positive for u0, u8, u10 and u14 and negative for u9 and u11.
answer.main_feature: The genuine nodule signal appears only as smaller localized departures from the stripe pattern near and just right of centre. These include rows 8-11 at cols 16-19 (where group-A units are strongly positive and group-B units strongly negative, so brightness there favours benign) and rows 12-17 at cols 9-13. These likely reflect nodule extent or density, but the model's decision is dominated by the global stripe detectors.
